- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or erratic, model often underestimates; increase forecast to align with downward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70.5), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction by 1–2% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; force mean reversion toward recent 7–14 day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; dampen volatility by smoothing with 14-day moving average of true values.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending downward, model undercorrects; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
